schemaClass.name: Action
schemaClass.description: An Action entity specifies the mechanism by which inputs are transformed into outputs.

schemaProperty.name: Percent Complete
schemaProperty.description: Percent Complete represents the percentage this Action is complete.

schemaProperty.name: Start
schemaProperty.description: Start represents the time when this Action begins.

schemaProperty.name: Duration
schemaProperty.description: Duration represents the period of time this Action occurs.

schemaClass.name: Artifact
schemaClass.description: An Artifact entity specifies a document or other source of information that is referenced by or generated in the knowledgebase.

schemaProperty.name: Date Published
schemaProperty.description: Date Published represents the date when this Artifact was accessed (webpage), published, or uploaded to the knowledgebase.

schemaProperty.name: File
schemaProperty.description: The File that represents this Artifact.

schemaClass.name: Asset
schemaClass.description: An Asset entity specifies an object, person, or organization that performs Actions, such as a system, subsystem, component, or element.

schemaClass.name: Resource
schemaClass.description: A Resource entity specifies a consumable or producible Asset.

schemaProperty.name: Units
schemaProperty.description: Units represents this Resource's units used to measure the amounts, such as each or tons.

schemaProperty.name: Initial Amount
schemaProperty.description: Initial Amount represents this Resource's starting amount.

schemaProperty.name: Minimum Amount
schemaProperty.description: Minimum Amount represents this Resource's minimum amount allowed.

schemaProperty.name: Maximum Amount
schemaProperty.description: Maximum Amount represents this Resource's maximum amount allowed.

schemaClass.name: Port
schemaClass.description: An interaction point of a block, specifying the input and output flow.

schemaProperty.name: Direction
schemaProperty.description: Direction represents the flow of data on this port.

schemaClass.name: Characteristic
schemaClass.description: A Characteristic entity specifies properties of an entity.

schemaProperty.name: Value
schemaProperty.description: Value represents this Characteristic's current value.

schemaProperty.name: Units
schemaProperty.description: Units represents this Characteristic's units used to measure the value, such as pounds or miles per hour.

schemaClass.name: Measure
schemaClass.description: A Measure entity specifies properties of measurements and measuring methodologies, including metrics.

schemaProperty.name: Projected Value
schemaProperty.description: Projected Value represents this Measure's expected value to be achieved with existing resources.

schemaProperty.name: Threshold Value
schemaProperty.description: Threshold Value represents the minimum acceptable value for this Measure.

schemaProperty.name: Objective Value
schemaProperty.description: Objective Value represents the goal for this Measure.

schemaProperty.name: Improvement Direction
schemaProperty.description: Improvement Direction represents the direction in that metric improvement occurs. It is the direction from the Threshold Value to the Objective Value.

schemaProperty.name: Tolerance
schemaProperty.description: Tolerance represents the percentage of the value that forms the positive and negative tolerance bands. Tolerance is used when Value represents the planned measure value at a given time.

schemaClass.name: Connection
schemaClass.description: A Connection entity specifies the mechanism relating Assets. This is an abstract class.

schemaClass.name: Conduit
schemaClass.description: A Conduit entity specifies the connection between Assets and has capacity and latency, which carries an Input/Output.

schemaProperty.name: Capacity
schemaProperty.description: Capacity represents the maximum rate supported by the Conduit. (Used in simulation as to add time delay by dividing the Input/Output size with the capacity value.)

schemaProperty.name: Latency
schemaProperty.description: Latency represents the time required to transmit the information or Input/Output entity over this Conduit. This value does not factor in any delays due to capacity limitations.

schemaProperty.name: Units
schemaProperty.description: Units represents this Conduit's units used to measure the capacity, such as bits per second or gallons per minute.

schemaClass.name: Logical
schemaClass.description: A Logical entity specifies relationship between Assets. It is primarily used in database schema development and entity-relationship diagrams.

schemaClass.name: Cost
schemaClass.description: A Cost entity specifies the outlay or expenditure (as of effort or sacrifice) made to achieve an objective associated with another entity.

schemaProperty.name: Amount
schemaProperty.description: Amount represents this Cost's value.

schemaProperty.name: Units
schemaProperty.description: Units represents this Cost's units used to measure the amount, such as $ or Euro.

schemaProperty.name: Rate
schemaProperty.description: Rate represents this Cost's billing rate.

schemaProperty.name: Category
schemaProperty.description: Category represents the part of the lifecycle for which the money is used (commonly called Color of Money). This matches the Federal Government (DoD) cost phases.

schemaProperty.name: Contract Type
schemaProperty.description: Contract Type represents this Cost way to identify the reimbursement structure (i.e. CPFF vs T&M).

schemaClass.name: Decision
schemaClass.description: A Decision entity specifies a challenge and its resolution.

schemaProperty.name: Justification
schemaProperty.description: Justification represents the reason and context for making this Decision.

schemaProperty.name: Assumptions
schemaProperty.description: Assumptions represents facts that are used as a basis for this Decision. These assumptions can be taken for granted by the decision maker.

schemaClass.name: Equation
schemaClass.description: An Equation entity specifies an equation (mathematical or logical) that can be used to describe a part of the model.

schemaProperty.name: Value
schemaProperty.description: Value represents this Equation's text.

schemaClass.name: Input/Output
schemaClass.description: An Input/Output entity specifies the information, data, or object input to, triggers, or output from an Action.

schemaProperty.name: Size
schemaProperty.description: Size represents the amount or proportion of this Input/Output, such as 100 as in 100 Gigabytes or number of entities (e.g. 10 as in 10 tokens).

schemaProperty.name: Units
schemaProperty.description: Units represents this Input/Output's units used to measure the size, such as Gigabyte or tokens.

schemaClass.name: Issue
schemaClass.description: An Issue entity specifies a bug, user story, or an epic.

schemaProperty.name: Status
schemaProperty.description: Status represents the current state of this Issue.

stringAttribute.value: Open

schemaProperty.name: Assignee
schemaProperty.description: Assignee represents the user(s) and/or team(s) responsible for the issue.

schemaProperty.name: Priority
schemaProperty.description: Priority represents the level of effect this issue is causing.

stringAttribute.value: Moderate

schemaClass.name: Location
schemaClass.description: A Location entity specifies where an entity resides.

schemaClass.name: Orbital
schemaClass.description: An Orbital entity specifies a location along an orbit around a celestial body.

schemaProperty.name: Apoapsis
schemaProperty.description: Apoapsis represents the point of greatest distance from the celestial body being orbited. For Earth, the term is apogee. For the Sun the term commonly used is aphelion. The Apoapsis must be specified with the Periapsis to characterize the orbital ellipse shape.

schemaProperty.name: Periapsis
schemaProperty.description: Periapsis represents the point of closest distance from the celestial body being orbited. For Earth, the term is perigee. For the Sun the term commonly used is perihelion. The Periapsis must be specified with the Apoapsis to characterize the orbital ellipse shape.

schemaProperty.name: Eccentricity
schemaProperty.description: Eccentricity represents the amount the orbit deviates from a perfect circle (0 being perfectly circular and 1 is a parabola - no longer a closed orbit). The Eccentricity must be specified with the Semimajor axis to characterize the orbital ellipse shape.

schemaProperty.name: Semimajor Axis
schemaProperty.description: Semimajor Axis represents the one half of the length of the longest diameter of the orbital ellipse. The Semimajor axis must be specified with the Eccentricity to characterize the orbital ellipse shape.

schemaProperty.name: Inclination
schemaProperty.description: Inclination represents the angle between the orbital plane and a reference plane, such as the equatorial plane for Earth. The Inclination must be specified with the Longitude of Ascending Node to characterize the orbital plane.

schemaProperty.name: Reference Plane
schemaProperty.description: Reference Plane represents the reference plane from where the Inclination angle will be calculated.

schemaProperty.name: Longitude of Ascending Node
schemaProperty.description: Longitude of Ascending Node represents the angle from the Origin of Longitude to the ascending node, measured in the Reference Plane. For the Earth, the origin of longitude is typically the Prime Meridian. The Longitude of Ascending Node must be specified with the Inclination to characterize the orbital plane.

schemaProperty.name: Origin of Longitude
schemaProperty.description: Origin of Longitude represents the reference meridian from where the Longitude of Ascending Node will be calculated.

schemaProperty.name: Argument of Periapsis
schemaProperty.description: Argument of Periapsis represents the angle between the Periapsis and the ascending node as measured in the orbital plane in the direction of motion.

schemaProperty.name: Mean Anomaly
schemaProperty.description: Mean Anomaly represents the proportion of orbital area swept since the last Periapsis at the specified time. It is used to define the position of the orbiting Asset along the orbital ellipse.

schemaClass.name: Physical
schemaClass.description: A Physical entity specifies a location on or above the surface.

schemaProperty.name: Address
schemaProperty.description: Address represents this Location's complete address.

schemaProperty.name: Coordinates
schemaProperty.description: Coordinates represents the coordinate points for this Location (GPS or other system).

schemaProperty.name: Altitude
schemaProperty.description: Altitude represents the distance above the surface.

schemaClass.name: Virtual
schemaClass.description: A Virtual entity specifies a location within a digital network.

schemaProperty.name: Address
schemaProperty.description: Address represents the identification address using the Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) protocols.

schemaClass.name: Risk
schemaClass.description: A Risk entity specifies the combined probability and consequence in achieving objectives.

schemaProperty.name: Consequence Description
schemaProperty.description: Consequence Description represents the result of this Risk occurring.

schemaProperty.name: Consequence
schemaProperty.description: Consequence represents the level of effect from this Risk occurring.

schemaProperty.name: Probability
schemaProperty.description: Probability represents the chance that this Risk will occur.

schemaProperty.name: Status
schemaProperty.description: Status represents the current state of this Risk.

stringAttribute.value: Open

schemaClass.name: Statement
schemaClass.description: A Statement entity specifies text referenced by the knowledgebase and usually contain in an Artifact.

schemaClass.name: Requirement
schemaClass.description: A Requirement entity identifies a capability, characteristic, or quality factor of a system that must exist for the system to have value and utility to the user.

schemaProperty.name: Rationale
schemaProperty.description: Rationale provides a place to capture the reason(s) behind this Requirement.

schemaProperty.name: Status
schemaProperty.description: Status represents the current state of this Requirement.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

schemaProperty.name: Quality Score
schemaProperty.description: The calculated quality score.

schemaProperty.name: Appropriate
schemaProperty.description: Appropriate represents if this Requirement expresses the specific intent and amount of detail of the need or requirement statement appropriate to the level (the level of abstraction, organization, or system architecture) of the entity to which it refers.

schemaProperty.name: Complete
schemaProperty.description: Complete represents if this Requirement sufficiently describes the necessary capability, characteristic, constraint, or quality factor to meet the need, source, or parent requirement from which it was transformed without needing other information to understand the requirement.

schemaProperty.name: Conforming
schemaProperty.description: Conforming represents if the Requirement is conforming to an approved standard pattern and style guide or standard for writing and managing needs and requirements.

schemaProperty.name: Correct
schemaProperty.description: Correct represents if this Requirement is an accurate representation of the need, source, or parent requirement from which it was transformed.

schemaProperty.name: Feasible
schemaProperty.description: Feasible represents if this Requirement can be realized within entity constraints with acceptable risk.

schemaProperty.name: Necessary
schemaProperty.description: Necessary represents if this Requirement defines an essential capability, characteristic, constraint, or quality factor needed to satisfy a lifecycle concept, need, source, or parent requirement.

schemaProperty.name: Verifiable
schemaProperty.description: Verifiable represents if this Requirement is provable (within realistic cost and schedule) that the system meets the requirement.

schemaProperty.name: Singular
schemaProperty.description: Singular represents if this Requirement states a single capability, characteristic, constraint, or quality factor.

schemaProperty.name: Unambiguous
schemaProperty.description: Unambiguous represents if this Requirement is stated such that the requirement can be interpreted in only one way by all the intended stakeholders.

schemaClass.name: Time
schemaClass.description: A Time entity specifies a point or period when something occurs or during which an action, asset, process, or condition exists or continues.

schemaProperty.name: Start
schemaProperty.description: Start represents the time when this Time begins.

schemaProperty.name: Duration
schemaProperty.description: Duration represents the period of time this Time occurs.

schemaClass.name: Test Case
schemaClass.description: A Test Case entity represents a set of conditions utilized to determine whether a system works as intended.

schemaProperty.name: Set Up
schemaProperty.description: Set Up represents the prerequisites that must be fulfilled before executing this Test Case.

schemaProperty.name: Expected Result
schemaProperty.description: Expected Result represents the result expected when executing this Test Case.

schemaProperty.name: Actual Result
schemaProperty.description: Actual Results represents the results that are captured after executing a Test Case.

schemaProperty.name: Status
schemaProperty.description: Status represents the current state of this Test Case.

schemaClass.name: Task
schemaClass.description: A Task entity specifies an Action that must be completed for a particular project. It served as a "To-Do" for the Project.

schemaClass.name: Dependency
schemaClass.description: A Dependency entity specifies a connection between two Tasks in a Gantt Chart. It defines the relationship a Task depends on another Task in order to Start or Finish

schemaClass.name: Transition
schemaClass.description: A Transition entity specifies an action that, once completed, transitions one state (Characteristic) to another state (Characteristic).

label.name: Independent Verification & Validation Plan Document
label.description: Independent approach to verification and validation (IV&V) Plan documents the approach and processes that will be used to ensure that an independent approach to the verification and validation is incorporated into the project from the beginning of the lifecycle through implementation.

label.name: Test Plan Document
label.description: The Test Plan document documents and tracks the necessary information required to effectively define the approach to be used in the testing of the project's product.

label.name: Integrated Logistics Support Plan Document
label.description: The Integrated Logistics Support Plan (ILSP) serves as the master logistics planning document that describes necessary logistic activities, assigns responsibility for those activities, and establishes a schedule for completion.

label.name: Standard Operating Procedure Document
label.description: A Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is a set of step by step instructions for carrying out a specific technique. They can be used for any technique, but this guide focuses on their use in documenting monitoring techniques, specifically for species and ecological communities.

label.name: Concept of Operations Document
label.description: The Concept of Operations Document (CONOPS) is both an analysis and a formal document that describes how an asset, system, or capability will be employed and supported.

label.name: Requirements Document
label.description: The Requirements Document provides the stakeholders with a clear statement of the capabilities required of the system in order to solve the stakeholder's needs.

label.name: Simulation Output
label.description: Is the dashboard from an executed simulation.

label.name: Project Management Plan Document
label.description: The Project Management Plan (PMP) is a formal document used to document planning assumptions and decisions, facilitate communication among staekholders, and document approved scope, cost, and schedule baslines.

label.name: Final State
label.description: A UML State Machine's final state.

label.name: Initial State
label.description: A UML State Machine's initial state.

label.name: Report
label.description: System generated reports contain this label.

entity.name: Provide Authorized PANTRI Interaction State to Restaurant Staff
entity.description: The PANTRI System shall provide Authorized PANTRI Interaction State to the Restaurant Staff.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Rationale: Restaurant staff need service and scoped task authorization to enter operational records while remaining outside manager purchasing authority. This supplement makes the P-IO.17 staff-recipient obligation explicit instead of assuming that the PANTRI Staff output covers restaurant staff. Upstream stakeholder requirements: SR.12, SR.13. MOP: Restaurant Staff interaction-state agreement with the proposed restaurant/role/task/service matrix, paired with legitimate record-entry completion. Proposed verification criterion: P-F.0 provides the applicable P-IO.17 state to P-F.2 for each proposed fixture. Authorized available receipt/usage/count/waste entry succeeds. Another restaurant's record access, staff purchase approval and unavailable-service entry return denied/unavailable state and do not create an accepted record or purchase approval. Compare the returned state and resulting action with an independent matrix. The state does not claim control over physical receiving or food preparation. Method: Recipient contract test and authorization-state inspection. Scenario scope: Authorized record entry; Wrong restaurant; Staff attempts purchase approval; Unavailable service. Evaluation status: Planned, not executed. Fixture definitions are proposed review assumptions; operational agreement is not claimed. Requirement status: Draft.

entity.name: Mismatch between approved and transmitted order versions
entity.description: Condition: A draft can change between review, approval and handoff, or a send operation can be repeated. Event: A stale or different order version is transmitted, or a previously sent order is transmitted again without the intended transaction controls. Consequence: The restaurant may be committed to quantities the manager did not approve, violating purchasing authority under SR.03 and SR.03A. Basis: The existing synthetic path demonstrates a single controlled sequence; concurrency, network retries and external acceptance are not established. Mitigation: Associate approval with an explicit order version, compare final identifiers and quantities at handoff, reject unapproved/superseded drafts and define repeated-send behavior. Test changed versions, missing approval and repeated actions. Trigger: The outgoing payload differs from the approved version or a transaction identifier has already been accepted. Residual risk: An external supplier may process retries differently; an agreed external transaction contract is still needed. Status: Open. Qualitative ratings are preliminary, not measured probabilities.

stringAttribute.value: Open

entity.name: Administer and Support PANTRI Operation
entity.description: PANTRI Staff function: establish agreed operating/access/retention rules, monitor service and exception information, coordinate follow-up, and authorize recovery or handover. Operational policy values remain proposed until confirmed.

entity.name: Review current ingredient inventory
entity.description: PANTRI shall present the Restaurant Manager with a restaurant-specific inventory view identifying each selected ingredient's recorded quantity, unit, batch, recorded expiration information, and last update time.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Purchase planning must distinguish recorded inventory from a fresh physical count. Owner: Restaurant Manager. Parent need: N.01. MOE V.01: At least 90% of representative review tasks identify usable recorded stock and missing or stale information without assistance. Selection reason: Correct interpretation supports purchasing decisions. Planned validation: Prepared inventory and batch cases including stale updates and missing expiration values. Targets are proposed; validation is not performed. Draft text-quality review: Appropriate, Complete, Conforming, Necessary, Singular, Unambiguous and Verifiable are supported by the statement plus the stated acceptance criteria and source-need trace. Correct and Feasible remain No pending stakeholder confirmation and feasibility evidence; these flags are not claims of disproved correctness or failed implementation. Validation is still planned.

entity.name: Provide Joint Waste and Availability Measures
entity.description: The PANTRI System shall provide Joint Waste and Availability Measures to the Restaurant Manager.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Rationale: The P-IO.10 exchange supports SR.06. Waste mass per 100 diner covers and ingredient stockout rate for the same restaurant, ingredient scope and evaluation period, with missing/zero denominator treatment stated Upstream stakeholder requirements: SR.06. MOP: Waste-mass-per-100-covers and ingredient-stockout-rate calculation agreement with an independently computed decimal reference using the proposed observation dictionary, scope and display precision. Proposed verification criterion: Both metrics use the identical declared restaurant, selected-ingredient scope and period. Under the proposed fixture definition, 10 kg waste/200 covers yields 5.00 kg per 100 covers; 2 unavailable ingredient-demand opportunities/100 observed opportunities yields 2.00%. Compare independently calculated values at the proposed two-decimal test display precision. Missing observations or zero denominators yield an explicit not-calculable result and reason, not zero. Show metric denominators and coverage so reduced observation cannot masquerade as improvement. Method: Independent calculation analysis and output test. Scenario scope: Known totals; Zero covers; Zero stockout-opportunity denominator; Missing observation interval; Different restaurant/period; Waste decreases while stockouts increase. Evaluation status: Planned, not executed. Fixture definitions are proposed review assumptions; operational agreement is not claimed. Requirement status: Draft.

entity.name: Approved Orders & Delivery Information
entity.description: The PANTRI System shall interface with the Ingredient Supplier through the Approved Orders & Delivery Information.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Rationale: The supplier conduit transfers approved purchasing intent outward and associated confirmation/delivery/exception information inward. Keeping the two directions distinct preserves the approved order while avoiding a false equivalence between transmission, supplier confirmation and physical delivery. Upstream stakeholder requirements: SR.03, SR.04, SR.11. MOP: Approved-order and interaction-state preservation outward through P-IO.11/.17; supplier-event association and field preservation inward through P-IO.05. Proposed verification criterion: Use proposed bidirectional fixtures: P-F.0-to-P-F.3 orders carry restaurant/order/version, ingredient identifiers, quantities and units; P-F.3-to-P-F.0 events carry the matching order, event type/time and applicable confirmation/delivery/exception context. Compare both with independent approval and event ledgers. Accept valid associated exchanges; reject a missing order reference or wrong restaurant. Preserve pending state when no valid response arrives. Duplicates follow the declared proposed rule and do not manufacture confirmation or delivery. Method: Bidirectional interface contract test and ledger inspection. Scenario scope: Approved order and associated confirmation; Partial/delayed event; Missing order reference; Wrong restaurant/order; Duplicate message; No response. Evaluation status: Planned, not executed. Fixture definitions are proposed review assumptions; operational agreement is not claimed. Requirement status: Draft.

entity.name: Provide Operational Record Acknowledgments
entity.description: The PANTRI System shall provide Operational Record Acknowledgments to the Restaurant Staff.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Rationale: The P-IO.14 exchange supports SR.07, SR.08, SR.09, SR.10. Accepted/rejected entry results and retained record identifiers or correction references. An acknowledgment certifies processing of a record, not the truth of a physical measurement Upstream stakeholder requirements: SR.07, SR.08, SR.09, SR.10. MOP: Acknowledgment outcome, originating staff-context and retained record/correction-reference agreement, paired with the existing receiving, usage, correction-history and waste-field preservation measures. Proposed verification criterion: Each prepared entry attempt returns the correct accepted/rejected result to the originating authorized staff context. Accepted results identify the retained record or correction; rejected results do not claim a retained record. Compare the acknowledgment with an independently specified expected result and the retained record/history. Preserve the existing type-specific quantity, unit, time, reason and explicit-unknown criteria. A later correction retains earlier history; another restaurant receives neither the acknowledgment nor its protected record identifiers. Method: Acknowledgment contract test and retained-record/history inspection. Scenario scope: Accepted receipt/usage/waste; Rejected invalid entry; Accepted linked correction; Second correction; Unknown batch/expiration; Wrong restaurant context. Evaluation status: Planned, not executed. Fixture definitions are proposed review assumptions; operational agreement is not claimed. Requirement status: Draft.

Upstream stakeholder requirements: SR.11, SR.12. MOP: Completeness and association accuracy of exception transaction, ownership, state and follow-up information. Agreement of recorded service availability/unavailability observations with the workflow-check reference log. Proposed verification criterion: Each prepared supply/collection exception retains the affected transaction, restaurant, responsible party, current state and recorded action/resolution; unresolved cases remain unresolved. Service-monitoring scenarios also retain the affected workflow, restaurant scope, observed state and observation time consistently with the independent check log; missing observations are explicit and do not imply availability. Method: Test and demonstration. Scenario scope: Supply delay; Collection delay; Partial fulfillment; Unassigned follow-up; Resolution without physical-completion evidence. Proposed verification criterion: In proposed fixtures, route manager requests/revisions/approvals from P-F.1 to P-F.0 and inventory/advice/metrics/status/interaction-state outputs back to the authorized manager boundary. Preserve restaurant and task, draft/order version, ingredient quantities/units or metric scope/period as applicable. Compare each direction with independent message fixtures. Accept a valid scoped exchange; reject a missing mandatory association or wrong restaurant/task without leakage or unintended approval. Every listed message category has at least one valid and one adverse case. Method: Bidirectional interface contract test and message inspection. Scenario scope: Valid request and information response; Valid revision and explicit approval; Missing draft/version; Wrong restaurant; Unauthorized task; Pending external status. entity.description: The PANTRI System shall interface with the Restaurant Staff through the Receiving, Usage, Inventory & Waste Information.

entity.name: Preserve Confirmed Records Through Recovery
entity.description: PANTRI shall restore 100% of the confirmed records in the prepared interruption-recovery reference scenario with their required identifiers, quantities, units, approvals, corrections and relationships intact.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Rationale: Approvals, corrections and transaction links must survive interruption so that restored records remain usable and auditable under SR.14. Restoring field values without their relationships would not preserve the operational evidence needed for subsequent decisions and recovery follow-up. Upstream stakeholder requirements: SR.14. MOS: Record integrity rate = 100 times confirmed reference records with every required field preserved divided by all confirmed reference records. Relationship integrity rate = 100 times required reference relationships restored with correct endpoints and type divided by all required reference relationships. Both rates must be 100%. Proposed validation criterion: Prepare at least 50 confirmed linked records and an independently retained reference snapshot/relationship manifest before interruption. Include multiple restaurants, receipts, usage, waste, successive corrections, approvals and associated transaction records. After restoration, compare identifiers, quantities, units, decisions and every required relationship; both integrity rates must equal 100%. Cross-restaurant associations and missing/dangling links fail. Record elapsed restoration time and discrepancy logs. No agreed recovery-time limit, recovery-point objective or production resilience achievement is inferred. Method: Planned interruption-and-restoration validation with independent record and relationship reconciliation. Scenario scope: Complete linked recovery; Missing record; Changed quantity/unit; Missing approval/correction link; Wrong restaurant association; Repeated restoration. Evaluation status: Planned, not executed. Fixture definitions are proposed review assumptions; operational agreement is not claimed. Requirement status: Draft.

entity.name: Associate recovery responses
entity.description: The PANTRI System shall associate each accepted recovery response with its identified recovery request.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Rationale: Recovery information must remain tied to the request. Higher-level source: SR.11; P-SFR.01. Allocated function: P-F.0.4.2. MOP: Response-to-request association agreement. Proposed verification criterion: Use valid, unknown-request and repeated response fixtures; only a valid associated response changes recorded request state and repeated receipt remains identifiable. Method: Test. Verification status: Planned; no implementation or operational acceptance result is inferred from the architecture model.

entity.name: Record Explicit Purchase Approval
entity.description: Leaf function within P-F.0.3 Coordinate Approved Ingredient Orders. Its obligations and verification are specified by the associated P-AFR requirement.

entity.name: Accept Supplier Confirmation Delivery and Exception Information
entity.description: The PANTRI System shall accept Supplier Confirmation Delivery and Exception Information from the Ingredient Supplier.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Rationale: Supplier messages support SR.04 and SR.11 only when associated with the correct approved order. Confirmation, delivery information and exceptions must remain distinguishable. If no valid associated supplier response has been received, the order remains unconfirmed. Upstream stakeholder requirements: SR.04, SR.11. MOP: P-IO.05 accepted-message field and order-association agreement; rejection of malformed/unrelated supplier messages at P-F.3-to-P-F.0. Proposed verification criterion: Use proposed supplier fixtures containing restaurant/order reference, event identifier, event type, occurrence time and applicable confirmed quantity/unit, delivery or exception information. Accept a valid associated event unchanged; reject an unknown order, restaurant mismatch or missing required event context without altering another transaction. Compare retained events with an independent event ledger. Duplicate behavior follows the declared proposed deduplication rule. An absent response must not be represented as confirmation or physical delivery. Method: Boundary test and event-ledger inspection. Scenario scope: Confirmation; Partial confirmation; Delayed delivery report; Exception; Unknown order; Duplicate event; No response. Evaluation status: Planned, not executed. Fixture definitions are proposed review assumptions; operational agreement is not claimed. Requirement status: Draft.

entity.name: Recorded Supplier Order State
entity.description: First-level internal exchange. Source: [3]; destination: [5]; receiving ICOM role: I. Fields: restaurant_id, order_id, state, confirmation_reference, delivery_information, exceptions. Quantities carry explicit units. Missing values remain explicit. Errors are returned with transaction/task association; no false success is inferred. Draft contract v1.0.0.

entity.name: Transmit only the approved final order
entity.description: The PANTRI System shall transmit a purchase order only when its restaurant identifier, final version, ingredient identifiers, quantities and units agree with its explicit manager approval record.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Rationale: The supplier must receive the authorized version unchanged. Higher-level source: SR.03; P-SFR.01. Allocated function: P-F.0.3.3. MOP: Unauthorized transmissions and approved-to-sent discrepancies. Proposed verification criterion: Unapproved, revised-after-approval and wrong-restaurant cases produce zero handoffs; a valid 5/6/1 kg approval produces an exactly matching supplier payload. Duplicate attempts do not create a second commitment. Method: Test. Verification status: Planned; no implementation or operational acceptance result is inferred from the architecture model.

entity.name: Evaluate 1.2.8 Provide Exception and Service Monitoring Information
entity.description: Requirement: 1.2.8. The PANTRI System shall provide Exception and Service Monitoring Information to the PANTRI Staff. Method: Test and demonstration. Measure: Completeness and association accuracy of exception transaction, ownership, state and follow-up information. Agreement of recorded service availability/unavailability observations with the workflow-check reference log. Procedure: prepare the reference inputs and expected results independently; execute valid, boundary and adverse scenarios; compare observations with the criterion; retain logs and discrepancies. No execution is claimed.

stringAttribute.value: Not Run

Each prepared supply/collection exception retains the affected transaction, restaurant, responsible party, current state and recorded action/resolution; unresolved cases remain unresolved. Service-monitoring scenarios also retain the affected workflow, restaurant scope, observed state and observation time consistently with the independent check log; missing observations are explicit and do not imply availability.

A stable model baseline and implementation build; agreed scope and policy values; independent reference records. Scenario set: Supply delay; Collection delay; Partial fulfillment; Unassigned follow-up; Resolution without physical-completion evidence
Not executed. No pass/fail result or operational validation evidence is available for this planned case.

entity.description: PANTRI shall retain an exception record identifying its affected order or collection request, restaurant, responsible party, current state, and recorded follow-up or resolution.

entity.name: Govern PANTRI Service Continuity
entity.description: Apply task authorization, observe service and exceptions, restore confirmed records and export authorized handover records.

entity.name: Restore confirmed linked records
entity.description: The PANTRI System shall restore confirmed operational records and their required approval and correction relationships from the selected authorized recovery snapshot.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Rationale: Restored files alone do not establish semantic integrity. Higher-level source: SR.14; P-SFR.01. Allocated function: P-F.0.6.3. MOP: Restored record and relationship integrity rates. Proposed verification criterion: Compare recovery output with an independent record and link manifest; both integrity rates are 100% for the declared fixture. No agreed recovery-time or recovery-point objective is inferred. Method: Test. Verification status: Planned; no implementation or operational acceptance result is inferred from the architecture model.

entity.name: Check Missing Ingredient Information
entity.description: Team16 plan A supporting step within the original UC.1, after UC.1.9 and before UC.1.10. The manager checks recorded quantity, unit and expiration-date completeness, flags missing quantity or unknown expiration, and reviews the basis of the proposed purchase. Unknown is never treated as zero quantity or confirmed usable stock. If the basis remains insufficient, the manager defers approval and returns to information review; no approval or supplier transmission is authorized by this check. Actual count corrections remain UC.7. The normal continuation to UC.1.10 applies only when the manager elects to continue review/revision. Functional responsibility: external P-F.1; this is not a new PANTRI architecture function.

entity.name: Provide Operating Hour Workflow Availability
entity.description: PANTRI shall make the approved operational workflows available for at least 99% of the pilot restaurants' agreed operating time.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Rationale: Availability during operating hours is necessary because interruption of planning, order and record workflows can prevent time-sensitive ingredient decisions under SR.12. A restaurant-specific assessment avoids hiding one pilot restaurant's disruption inside a combined service average. Upstream stakeholder requirements: SR.12. MOS: For each restaurant, 100 times (agreed operating minutes minus PANTRI-unavailable minutes) divided by agreed operating minutes. The proposed acceptance interpretation is at least 99% for every pilot restaurant, with any pooled rate reported separately. Proposed validation criterion: During the proposed 28-day pilot, evaluate every restaurant against its declared operating calendar and approved workflow set. Proposed accounting counts an in-scope interval unavailable when any required workflow cannot complete because of PANTRI. Report each restaurant's numerator, denominator, outages and observation gaps; require at least 99% availability per restaurant. Fix sampling, outage start/end inference and exclusions before execution. Missing observation coverage prevents a conformance conclusion and is not automatically counted as available time. Method: Planned operational validation through scheduled representative workflow checks and independent outage-log reconciliation. Scenario scope: All required workflows available; One required workflow unavailable; Restaurant-specific outage; Outside agreed hours; Maintenance under declared rule; Missing observations. Evaluation status: Planned, not executed. Fixture definitions are proposed review assumptions; operational agreement is not claimed. Requirement status: Draft.

entity.name: Planning and Information Requests
entity.description: Restaurant and selected-ingredient scope, requested planning/information task, period and relevant demand context. Requests enable the requested interaction; they do not approve purchases.

entity.name: Verify P-AFR.08 Version quantity revisions
entity.description: Revise beef from 4 to 5 kg in the prepared 4/6/1 kg draft; the revised version is 5/6/1 kg, remains unapproved and produces no transmission. Invalid quantities are rejected.

stringAttribute.value: Not Run
All applicable technical criteria hold; retain observed values and discrepancy records.

Use the declared independent fixture and oracle. Revise beef from 4 to 5 kg in the prepared 4/6/1 kg draft; the revised version is 5/6/1 kg, remains unapproved and produces no transmission. Invalid quantities are rejected.

Missing values remain explicit. Errors are returned with transaction/task association; no false success is inferred. Draft contract v1.0.0.

Quantities carry explicit units. Missing values remain explicit. Errors are returned with transaction/task association; no false success is inferred. Draft contract v1.0.0.

entity.name: Transfer operational records for handover
entity.description: PANTRI shall provide an authorized handover export that preserves the identifiers, quantities, units, and recorded decision history of the selected restaurant operational records.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Owner: PANTRI Staff. Parent need: N.14. Life-cycle retirement requires usable controlled transfer. MOE V.15: 100% of selected handover records reconciled by authorized reviewer. Reason: tests usable transfer, not file generation alone. Validation: export representative recovery record set in agreed readable format; compare required fields and linked identifiers; report lost context. Acceptance targets remain proposed; validation is planned, not performed. Draft text-quality review: Appropriate, Complete, Conforming, Necessary, Singular, Unambiguous and Verifiable are supported by the statement plus the stated acceptance criteria and source-need trace. Correct and Feasible remain No pending stakeholder confirmation and feasibility evidence; these flags are not claims of disproved correctness or failed implementation. Validation is still planned.

entity.name: Provide Approved Purchase Orders
entity.description: The PANTRI System shall provide Approved Purchase Orders to the Ingredient Supplier.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Rationale: The P-IO.11 exchange supports SR.03. Final orders associated with explicit manager approval. Ingredient identifiers, quantities and units remain unchanged between the approved version and outgoing supplier payload Upstream stakeholder requirements: SR.03. MOP: Approved-to-transmitted order agreement and unapproved-transmission rejection, paired with successful transmission of valid approved orders Proposed verification criterion: Every prepared valid explicitly approved order reaches the supplier boundary with the same approved order version, ingredient identifiers, quantities and units as the independently retained approval snapshot. Unapproved, superseded or wrong-restaurant drafts are blocked. Repeated-send behavior follows the declared proposed transaction rule and cannot silently create a second independent commitment. Record handoff separately from supplier confirmation or physical fulfillment. Method: Test and event inspection. Scenario scope: Valid approved order; Unapproved draft; Changed/superseded version; Wrong restaurant/session; Repeated send; Unit preservation. Evaluation status: Planned, not executed. Fixture definitions are proposed review assumptions; operational agreement is not claimed. Requirement status: Draft.

entity.name: Support Authorized Use Without Cross Restaurant Access
entity.description: PANTRI shall enforce the agreed restaurant and task authorization policy so that all prepared unauthorized-access scenarios are denied while at least 95% of legitimate role-specific tasks succeed.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Rationale: Restaurant and task boundaries protect operational records and purchasing authority under SR.13. Pairing denial with legitimate completion prevents a design that blocks everyone from satisfying the access requirement while leaving intended restaurant work unusable. Upstream stakeholder requirements: SR.13. MOS: Unauthorized rejection rate = 100 times correctly denied prepared unauthorized scenarios divided by all prepared unauthorized scenarios. Legitimate completion rate = 100 times successfully completed prepared authorized role-specific tasks divided by all prepared authorized tasks. Report both denominators and per-role/restaurant results. Proposed validation criterion: Use a proposed, predeclared restaurant/role/action matrix covering all pilot restaurants and relevant actor tasks. Deny every prepared unauthorized scenario and complete at least 95% of the prepared legitimate task set. Compare access decisions and resulting record/order effects with independently specified matrix expectations; a denied task must not leak records or perform the action. Denominators must be nonzero and fixed before execution. Report incomplete observations separately; do not generalize this bounded result to all security threats. Method: Planned scenario-based suitability validation with representative role-specific task execution and independent policy-matrix comparison. Scenario scope: Legitimate manager/staff tasks; Cross-restaurant access; Staff purchase approval; Authorized scoped support; Unauthorized supplier/recovery task; Legitimate task blocked. Evaluation status: Planned, not executed. Fixture definitions are proposed review assumptions; operational agreement is not claimed. Requirement status: Draft.

Rationale: Managers must be able to assess advice. Higher-level source: SR.02; P-SFR.01. Allocated function: P-F.0.2.2. MOP: Advice basis field coverage and agreement. Proposed verification criterion: Compare each prepared recommendation to independently specified demand, stock, horizon and limitation facts; all applicable basis fields agree. Method: Test. Verification status: Planned; no implementation or operational acceptance result is inferred from the architecture model.

entity.name: Service Policies and Authorized Support Commands
entity.description: Agreed operating hours, role/restaurant permissions, planning/retention rules and authorized support/recovery/handover commands. Unconfirmed values stay proposed; demo defaults do not become operational policy.

entity.name: Maintain Ingredient Operational Records
entity.description: Capture and retain actual restaurant events, queries and transaction history without claiming physical receiving or disposal.

entity.name: Restaurant Manager Reviews Inventory Status
entity.description: Team16 plan B is incorporated as a supporting path in this original inventory-status use case. The manager may request retained correction history with the inventory view. Show prior/new quantity, unit, reason, responsible user and time; order multiple corrections and show an explicit no-history result. The operation is read-only. Actor: Restaurant Manager, already allocated in the baseline. Software execution is not claimed.

entity.name: Evaluate 1.3.4 System Operation & Support Information
entity.description: Planned evaluation for 1.3.4. Method: Bidirectional interface contract test and support-record inspection. MOP: P-IO.07 inbound command/policy scope and version agreement; P-IO.15-.17 outbound monitoring, recovered/exported-record and interaction-state agreement. Proposed criterion: In proposed P-F.5-to-P-F.0 fixtures, policies/commands preserve authorized actor, restaurant/task scope, version/effective context and referenced recovery/export set. Reverse fixtures preserve exception/workflow ID, observation time/state and recovered/exported record references as applicable. Compare both directions with independent policy, monitoring and record fixtures. Valid authorized exchanges succeed; missing scope, wrong role or unrelated restaurant is denied. Command acceptance is distinct from completed restoration/export; missing monitoring observations do not imply availability. Scenario scope: Valid policy and monitoring exchange; Authorized recovery/export; Missing scope; Wrong role/restaurant; Missing observation; Unavailable service. Evidence to retain: declared fixture manifest, independent expected results, observed payload/state/output and discrepancy log. Status: Not Run. No execution result or operational agreement is claimed.

entity.name: Provide Inventory and Expiration Information
entity.description: The PANTRI System shall provide Inventory and Expiration Information to the Restaurant Manager.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Derivation: The P-IO.08 exchange supports SR.01, SR.05. Restaurant-specific recorded ingredient/batch quantity, unit, update time, known/unknown expiration and horizon-based alerts. This reports recorded information rather than physical freshness certification. Upstream stakeholder requirements: SR.01, SR.05. MOP: Agreement of displayed ingredient, quantity, unit, batch, expiration/unknown marker and update time with a reference record set. Classification agreement against a reference set evaluated with a declared horizon and date-boundary rule. Proposed verification criterion: Every mandatory field in each prepared complete record agrees exactly with the reference; absent or stale information retains the corresponding marker. Every prepared in-horizon and out-of-horizon record is classified according to the declared rule; unknown dates remain unknown. The operational horizon and boundary policy require confirmation before baselining. Method: Test and inspection; Test and analysis. Scenario scope: Complete batch; Unknown expiration; Missing or stale stock; Different restaurant; Horizon lower boundary; Upper boundary; Outside horizon; Unknown date; Already expired record. Evaluation status: Planned, not executed. Source targets and operational agreements remain proposed. Requirement status: Draft.

Use the declared independent fixture and oracle. Inspect inventory, advice, expiration and paired-metric views against independent expected payloads; all applicable basis and limitation fields are visible.

entity.name: Verify P-AFR.07 Calculate paired waste and availability measures
entity.description: Recompute W=100*waste_mass_kg/covers [kg/100 covers] and S=100*unavailable_valid_opportunities/all_valid_opportunities [%]. Use fractional fixtures and tolerance max(1e-9,1e-9*abs(expected)). Missing/zero denominators yield null. Verify restaurant, ingredient and period association separately. See Set Up and Expected Result. Full verification remains Not Run.

stringAttribute.value: Not Run

W and S equal independent values within max(1e-9,1e-9*abs(expected)); units are kg/100 covers and percent respectively. Missing/zero denominators yield null. Scope identifiers agree in the integration fixture. All criteria are required before marking this full procedure passed.

Prepare independent expected values for waste 1 kg / 3 covers and stockout 1 / 3 opportunities, plus fractional 0.125 kg / 25 covers and 1 / 8 opportunities. Include zero, missing and null denominators. Associate both measures with the same restaurant, ingredient scope and evaluation period in a separate integration fixture. Preserve fixture inputs before running.

entity.name: Recover confirmed operational records
entity.description: PANTRI shall restore confirmed operational records after a service interruption with their identifiers, quantities, units, approvals, corrections, and relationships intact.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Owner: PANTRI Staff. Parent need: N.14. Recovery must preserve decision evidence. MOE V.14: 100% of prepared confirmed records and links restored intact. Reason: data integrity, not mere backup existence. Validation: >=50 linked inventory, usage, waste, order and exception records; simulate interruption and compare. Restoration time is recorded; recovery-time target awaits stakeholder agreement. Acceptance targets remain proposed; validation is planned, not performed. Draft text-quality review: Appropriate, Complete, Conforming, Necessary, Singular, Unambiguous and Verifiable are supported by the statement plus the stated acceptance criteria and source-need trace. Correct and Feasible remain No pending stakeholder confirmation and feasibility evidence; these flags are not claims of disproved correctness or failed implementation. Validation is still planned.

entity.name: Apply scoped task authorization
entity.description: The PANTRI System shall deny a task when its actor role, restaurant scope or requested action is outside the declared authorization policy.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Rationale: All functions must respect restaurant and task boundaries. Higher-level source: SR.13; P-SFR.01. Allocated function: P-F.0.6.1. MOP: Unauthorized task success count. Proposed verification criterion: Compare allowed and denied prepared tasks against an independently declared policy matrix; every unauthorized task is blocked without data disclosure or mutation. This bounded test is not a complete security assessment. Method: Test. Verification status: Planned; no implementation or operational acceptance result is inferred from the architecture model.

entity.name: Authorized Recovery Disposition
entity.description: First-level internal exchange. Source: [6]; destination: [4]; receiving ICOM role: I. Fields: restaurant_id, request_id, command_id, authorized_disposition. Quantities carry explicit units. Missing values remain explicit. Errors are returned with transaction/task association; no false success is inferred. Draft contract v1.0.0.

entity.name: Evaluate 1.2.5 Provide Waste Collection Requests
entity.description: Requirement: 1.2.5. The PANTRI System shall provide Waste Collection Requests to the Recovery Partner. Method: Output contract test and inspection. Measure: Agreement of the outgoing collection-request fields and transaction association with an independent reference request. Procedure: prepare the reference inputs and expected results independently; execute valid, boundary and adverse scenarios; compare observations with the criterion; retain logs and discrepancies. No execution is claimed.

stringAttribute.value: Not Run

Every prepared valid request is provided to the Recovery Partner with the same restaurant/request identifier, recorded surplus or recovery context and required coordination information as the reference. A malformed, unrelated or unauthorized request is not silently forwarded. Sending a request does not mark physical collection complete or manufacture a partner response.

A stable model baseline and implementation build; agreed scope and policy values; independent reference records. Scenario set: Valid collection request; Missing request identifier; Wrong restaurant; Repeated request under agreed policy; No partner response
Not executed. No pass/fail result or operational validation evidence is available for this planned case.

entity.name: Recoverable and transferable records
entity.description:
I need trustworthy operational records to be recoverable after interruption and available for handover when the service is maintained or retired.
Owner: PANTRI Staff. Source: Operations, support, and retirement life-cycle concepts.

I need to record ingredient usage accurately during normal work without having to reconstruct it later.
Owner: Restaurant Staff. Source: UC.6.

entity.name: Accept Restaurant Operational Records
entity.description: The PANTRI System shall accept Restaurant Operational Records from the Restaurant Staff.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Rationale: Receiving, usage, counts/corrections, waste and demand observations supply the evidence for SR.01, SR.02 and SR.05-SR.10. Preserving record type, restaurant, quantities and occurrence context prevents unrelated observations or unknown values from becoming misleading planning inputs. Upstream stakeholder requirements: SR.01, SR.02, SR.05, SR.06, SR.07, SR.08, SR.09, SR.10. MOP: P-IO.04 required-field preservation and accepted/rejected record agreement for each proposed record type at the P-F.2-to-P-F.0 input boundary. Proposed verification criterion: Prepare independent receiving, usage, count/correction, waste, cover and stockout-observation fixtures under the proposed dictionary. Accept valid associated records with quantities, units and occurrence/update context intact; retain explicit unknown batch/expiration values. Reject missing type-specific mandatory fields, invalid quantities/units or another restaurant's submission without a new accepted record. Retain prior correction links. Each record type has a positive and an adverse case; saving a receipt does not assert physical-delivery completion. Method: Typed-record boundary test and retained-record inspection. Scenario scope: Complete receipt and unknown batch/expiration; Usage with missing unit; Second linked correction; Waste with recorded reason; Cover observation; Stockout opportunity observation; Wrong restaurant. Evaluation status: Planned, not executed. Fixture definitions are proposed review assumptions; operational agreement is not claimed. Requirement status: Draft.

entity.name: Evaluate P-NFR.02 Support Authorized Use Without Cross Restaurant Access
entity.description: Planned evaluation for P-NFR.02. Method: Planned scenario-based suitability validation with representative role-specific task execution and independent policy-matrix comparison. MOS: Unauthorized rejection rate = 100 times correctly denied prepared unauthorized scenarios divided by all prepared unauthorized scenarios. Legitimate completion rate = 100 times successfully completed prepared authorized role-specific tasks divided by all prepared authorized tasks. Report both denominators and per-role/restaurant results. Proposed criterion: Use a proposed, predeclared restaurant/role/action matrix covering all pilot restaurants and relevant actor tasks. Deny every prepared unauthorized scenario and complete at least 95% of the prepared legitimate task set. Compare access decisions and resulting record/order effects with independently specified matrix expectations; a denied task must not leak records or perform the action. Denominators must be nonzero and fixed before execution. Report incomplete observations separately; do not generalize this bounded result to all security threats. Scenario scope: Legitimate manager/staff tasks; Cross-restaurant access; Staff purchase approval; Authorized scoped support; Unauthorized supplier/recovery task; Legitimate task blocked. Evidence to retain: declared fixture manifest, independent expected results, observed payload/state/output and discrepancy log. Status: Not Run. No execution result or operational agreement is claimed.

entity.name: Evaluate 1.2.2 Provide Reviewable Purchasing Recommendations
entity.description: Requirement: 1.2.2. The PANTRI System shall provide Reviewable Purchasing Recommendations to the Restaurant Manager. Method: Test and inspection; Test. Measure: Completeness and numerical agreement of the recommendation basis with the selected scenario input and disclosed calculation. Agreement between accepted manager edits and the retained draft version before approval. Procedure: prepare the reference inputs and expected results independently; execute valid, boundary and adverse scenarios; compare observations with the criterion; retain logs and discrepancies. No execution is claimed.

stringAttribute.value: Not Run

All prepared recommendations identify expected demand, usable recorded inventory, horizon and material limitations; values reconcile with the selected input records. Every accepted edit is reflected in the draft; invalid edits leave the prior accepted draft intact; the revision event does not itself approve or transmit an order.

A stable model baseline and implementation build; agreed scope and policy values; independent reference records. Scenario set: Normal advice; Incomplete usage history; Unknown batch dates; Changed horizon; Beef 4 to 5 kg; Zero quantity; Negative or nonfinite quantity; Repeated edit; Revision after approval under agreed change policy
Not executed. No pass/fail result or operational validation evidence is available for this planned case.

entity.name: Provide Restaurant Ingredient Planning and Coordination
entity.description: The single top-level SoI function transforms restaurant records, purchasing requests and external transaction information into reviewable planning advice, approved-order exchanges, inventory/expiration and performance information, recovery coordination, exception follow-up and recoverable/handover records. Explicit manager approval and agreed service/access policies govern the function. Physical fulfillment, food preparation and waste processing remain external.

entity.name: Evaluate 1.3.2 Approved Orders & Delivery Information
entity.description: Planned evaluation for 1.3.2. Method: Bidirectional interface contract test and ledger inspection. MOP: Approved-order and interaction-state preservation outward through P-IO.11/.17; supplier-event association and field preservation inward through P-IO.05. Proposed criterion: Use proposed bidirectional fixtures: P-F.0-to-P-F.3 orders carry restaurant/order/version, ingredient identifiers, quantities and units; P-F.3-to-P-F.0 events carry the matching order, event type/time and applicable confirmation/delivery/exception context. Compare both with independent approval and event ledgers. Accept valid associated exchanges; reject a missing order reference or wrong restaurant. Preserve pending state when no valid response arrives. Duplicates follow the declared proposed rule and do not manufacture confirmation or delivery. Scenario scope: Approved order and associated confirmation; Partial/delayed event; Missing order reference; Wrong restaurant/order; Duplicate message; No response. Evidence to retain: declared fixture manifest, independent expected results, observed payload/state/output and discrepancy log. Status: Not Run. entity.name: Evaluate P-NFR.03 Preserve Confirmed Records Through Recovery
entity.description: Planned evaluation for P-NFR.03. Method: Planned interruption-and-restoration validation with independent record and relationship reconciliation. MOS: Record integrity rate = 100 times confirmed reference records with every required field preserved divided by all confirmed reference records. Relationship integrity rate = 100 times required reference relationships restored with correct endpoints and type divided by all required reference relationships. Both rates must be 100%. Proposed criterion: Prepare at least 50 confirmed linked records and an independently retained reference snapshot/relationship manifest before interruption. Include multiple restaurants, receipts, usage, waste, successive corrections, approvals and associated transaction records. After restoration, compare identifiers, quantities, units, decisions and every required relationship; both integrity rates must equal 100%. Cross-restaurant associations and missing/dangling links fail. Record elapsed restoration time and discrepancy logs. No agreed recovery-time limit, recovery-point objective or production resilience achievement is inferred. Scenario scope: Complete linked recovery; Missing record; Changed quantity/unit; Missing approval/correction link; Wrong restaurant association; Repeated restoration. Evidence to retain: declared fixture manifest, independent expected results, observed payload/state/output and discrepancy log. Status: Not Run. No execution result or operational agreement is claimed.

entity.name: Evaluate 1.1.4 Accept Restaurant Operational Records
entity.description: Planned evaluation for 1.1.4. Method: Typed-record boundary test and retained-record inspection. MOP: P-IO.04 required-field preservation and accepted/rejected record agreement for each proposed record type at the P-F.2-to-P-F.0 input boundary. Proposed criterion: Prepare independent receiving, usage, count/correction, waste, cover and stockout-observation fixtures under the proposed dictionary. Accept valid associated records with quantities, units and occurrence/update context intact; retain explicit unknown batch/expiration values. Reject missing type-specific mandatory fields, invalid quantities/units or another restaurant's submission without a new accepted record. Retain prior correction links. Each record type has a positive and an adverse case; saving a receipt does not assert physical-delivery completion. Scenario scope: Complete receipt and unknown batch/expiration; Usage with missing unit; Second linked correction; Waste with recorded reason; Cover observation; Stockout opportunity observation; Wrong restaurant. Evidence to retain: declared fixture manifest, independent expected results, observed payload/state/output and discrepancy log. Status: Not Run. No execution result or operational agreement is claimed.

entity.name: Scoped Planning Records
entity.description: First-level internal exchange. Source: [1]; destination: [2]; receiving ICOM role: I. Fields: restaurant_id, inventory, usage_history, expiration_dates, missing_fields, query_id. Quantities carry explicit units. Missing values remain explicit. Errors are returned with transaction/task association; no false success is inferred. Draft contract v1.0.0.

entity.name: Evaluate 1.1.3 Accept Explicit Purchase Approvals
entity.description: Planned evaluation for 1.1.3. Method: Boundary test and approval-event inspection. MOP: P-IO.03 approval-to-final-version association agreement and invalid-approval rejection at the P-F.1-to-P-F.0 control boundary. Proposed criterion: The proposed approval fixture identifies restaurant, approving manager, order/version and the final ingredient quantities/units or an immutable reference to that snapshot. Accept only a valid authorized approval of the current final version. Reject missing explicit approval, wrong restaurant and stale/version-mismatched approval without authorizing transmission. Compare the retained approval association with the independent approved snapshot; revision alone creates no approval. Scenario scope: Explicit current-version approval; Absent approval; Stale version; Wrong restaurant or role; Revision without approval. Evidence to retain: declared fixture manifest, independent expected results, observed payload/state/output and discrepancy log. Status: Not Run. No execution result or operational agreement is claimed.

entity.name: 2 Inventory Status and Correction History
entity.description: UC.2 scenario interaction 2, refinement of existing P-IO.08. No new architecture flow or endpoint. Restaurant and ingredient scope, request association and explicit no-history/missing-data outcomes are retained.

entity.name: Provide Reviewable Purchasing Recommendations
entity.description: The PANTRI System shall provide Reviewable Purchasing Recommendations to the Restaurant Manager.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Derivation: The P-IO.09 exchange supports SR.02, SR.03A. Proposed purchase quantities with expected demand, usable recorded stock, expiration horizon and material data limitations. Recommendations are drafts until explicit final approval. Upstream stakeholder requirements: SR.02, SR.03A. MOP: Completeness and numerical agreement of the recommendation basis with the selected scenario input and disclosed calculation. Agreement between accepted manager edits and the retained draft version before approval. Proposed verification criterion: All prepared recommendations identify expected demand, usable recorded inventory, horizon and material limitations; values reconcile with the selected input records. Every accepted edit is reflected in the draft; invalid edits leave the prior accepted draft intact; the revision event does not itself approve or transmit an order. Method: Test and inspection; Test. Scenario scope: Normal advice; Incomplete usage history; Unknown batch dates; Changed horizon; Beef 4 to 5 kg; Zero quantity; Negative or nonfinite quantity; Repeated edit; Revision after approval under agreed change policy. Evaluation status: Planned, not executed. Source targets and operational agreements remain proposed. Requirement status: Draft.

entity.name: Restaurant Staff Requirements
entity.description: Organizational group for SR.07-SR.10.

entity.name: Restaurant Operational Records
entity.description: Bundled restaurant records covering inventory/batches, actual receipts, historical usage, counts/corrections, waste events, diner-cover observations and proposed ingredient-demand/stockout observations. Preserve quantities, units, occurrence/update context and explicit unknown information. Proposed evaluation dictionary: each demand opportunity identifies restaurant, ingredient, period, opportunity ID, occurrence time, observed availability outcome and observation completeness. Stockout rate uses unavailable observed demand opportunities divided by all valid observed opportunities for the same declared scope and period. Zero stock alone does not establish a demand stockout. Missing observations or zero denominators yield not calculable. This dictionary is a proposed evaluation clarification, not a confirmed operational policy.

entity.name: Useful waste records
entity.description:
I need a clear record of the ingredient, amount, unit, and reason for food waste so the next planning cycle can use it.
Owner: Restaurant Staff. Source: UC.8.

entity.name: Restore Confirmed Records
