entity.name: Maintain operating-hour availability
entity.description: PANTRI shall make the approved operational workflows available for at least 99% of the pilot restaurants' agreed operating time.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Owner: PANTRI Staff. Parent need: N.12. Carries forward the preliminary 99% target; workflow completion, not page response, defines availability. MOE V.12: (agreed operating minutes - unavailable minutes) / agreed operating minutes >=99%. Reason: daily workflow continuity. Validation: agreed 28-day monitoring, predefined workflows, hours, intervals, maintenance and exclusions; report missing observations. Acceptance targets remain proposed; validation is planned, not performed. Draft text-quality review: Appropriate, Complete, Conforming, Necessary, Singular, Unambiguous and Verifiable are supported by the statement plus the stated acceptance criteria and source-need trace. Correct and Feasible remain No pending stakeholder confirmation and feasibility evidence; these flags are not claims of disproved correctness or failed implementation. Validation is still planned.

entity.name: Provide Restaurant Ingredient Planning and Coordination
entity.description: The PANTRI System shall provide restaurant ingredient planning and coordination.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Rationale: A single SoI obligation connects restaurant records to planning, purchasing authority, partner coordination and record continuity across the operational concept. Its detailed I/O and interface obligations make that broad function observable. The supplemental origin explains provenance; the operational dependencies explain why the requirement is necessary. Upstream stakeholder requirements: SR.01, SR.11, SR.15, SR.14, SR.10, SR.13, SR.03, SR.12, SR.02, SR.04, SR.05, SR.06, SR.07, SR.08, SR.09, SR.03A. MOP: Coverage and agreement of P-F.0 inputs, controls, outputs and interfaces with their individual acceptance records; count of passing detailed records divided by applicable detailed records. Proposed verification criterion: The proposed integrated fixture manifest includes every detailed functional/I/O/interface requirement and its valid, boundary and adverse scenarios. Every applicable detailed criterion passes; any exclusion is identified and justified before execution. Approval/version preservation, restaurant boundaries and pending external states remain intact across connected scenarios. Suitability is evaluated separately through P-NFR.01-P-NFR.03. Method: Integrated scenario test and allocation inspection. Scenario scope: Record-to-inventory/advice path; Revision-to-explicit-approval-to-transmission path; Supplier and recovery status paths; Service/access and recovery/handover paths. Evaluation status: Planned, not executed. Fixture definitions are proposed review assumptions; operational agreement is not claimed. Requirement status: Draft.

entity.name: Export scoped handover records
entity.description: The PANTRI System shall export the selected operational records and required relationships within the authorized restaurant handover scope.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Rationale: Retirement or transfer requires a usable scoped handover. Higher-level source: SR.15; P-SFR.01. Allocated function: P-F.0.6.4. MOP: Authorized export completeness and out-of-scope record count. Proposed verification criterion: Compare the export against an independent selected-scope manifest; all required records and links are present and out-of-scope records count is zero. Method: Test and inspection. Verification status: Planned; no implementation or operational acceptance result is inferred from the architecture model.

entity.name: Derive Purchasing Advice
entity.description: Leaf function within P-F.0.2 Derive Ingredient Planning Information. Its obligations and verification are specified by the associated P-AFR requirement.

entity.name: Verify P-AFR.13 Associate recovery responses
entity.description: Use valid, unknown-request and repeated response fixtures; only a valid associated response changes recorded request state and repeated receipt remains identifiable.

stringAttribute.value: Not Run
All applicable technical criteria hold; retain observed values and discrepancy records.

Use the declared independent fixture and oracle. Use valid, unknown-request and repeated response fixtures; only a valid associated response changes recorded request state and repeated receipt remains identifiable.

entity.name: Provide Authorized PANTRI Interaction State to Ingredient Supplier
entity.description: The PANTRI System shall provide Authorized PANTRI Interaction State to the Ingredient Supplier.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Rationale: The supplier boundary needs an explicit service and transaction/task authorization decision so that unrelated restaurant orders or responses cannot be exposed or accepted. This supplement states the supplier recipient of P-IO.17 separately from the native PANTRI Staff recipient. Upstream stakeholder requirements: SR.13, SR.12. MOP: Supplier interaction-state agreement with the proposed scoped order/task/service reference matrix, paired with legitimate transaction exchange completion. Proposed verification criterion: P-F.0 provides P-IO.17 to P-F.3 in the proposed supplier fixtures. A valid available scoped order/response exchange receives authorized state and succeeds. An unrelated restaurant/order, unauthorized task or unavailable service receives denied/unavailable state without exposing an unrelated order or accepting its response. Compare state and exchange outcome with the independent matrix. Authorization of information exchange does not establish supplier fulfillment. Method: Recipient contract test and boundary inspection. Scenario scope: Authorized scoped supplier exchange; Unrelated restaurant/order; Unauthorized task; Unavailable service. Evaluation status: Planned, not executed. Fixture definitions are proposed review assumptions; operational agreement is not claimed. Requirement status: Draft.

entity.name: Follow the approved order
entity.description: PANTRI shall present the current recorded confirmation, delivery, or exception status associated with each approved purchase order.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Owner: Restaurant Manager. Parent need: N.04. Approved requests differ from supplier confirmation; fulfillment remains external. MOE V.04: >=95% of review tasks identify recorded state and follow-up. Reason: measures information-system coordination. Validation: normal, partial, delayed and unconfirmed supplier cases; absent confirmation is not confirmation. Acceptance targets remain proposed; validation is planned, not performed. Draft text-quality review: Appropriate, Complete, Conforming, Necessary, Singular, Unambiguous and Verifiable are supported by the statement plus the stated acceptance criteria and source-need trace. Correct and Feasible remain No pending stakeholder confirmation and feasibility evidence; these flags are not claims of disproved correctness or failed implementation. Validation is still planned.

entity.name: Verify P-AFR.17 Present recorded transaction status
entity.description: Render pending, confirmed, partial, delayed and unresolved exception payloads; displayed state and references agree exactly with the underlying record.

stringAttribute.value: Not Run
All applicable technical criteria hold; retain observed values and discrepancy records.

Use the declared independent fixture and oracle. Render pending, confirmed, partial, delayed and unresolved exception payloads; displayed state and references agree exactly with the underlying record.

entity.name: Retain service and exception observations
entity.description: The PANTRI System shall retain the source function, task identifier, observation time and outcome for each received service observation.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Rationale: Monitoring needs observations rather than inferred availability. Higher-level source: SR.11, SR.12; P-SFR.01. Allocated function: P-F.0.6.2. MOP: Service observation field preservation rate. Proposed verification criterion: Inject successful and failed task observations from all five operational functions; retained records preserve source, time, task and outcome. Operating-hour availability remains a separate planned operational validation. Method: Test. Verification status: Planned; no implementation or operational acceptance result is inferred from the architecture model.

entity.name: PANTRI Function Architecture Requirements
entity.description: Derived functional requirements for Architecture Definition Function. Draft technical acceptance criteria. Operational stakeholder validation remains planned.

entity.name: Current ingredient visibility
entity.description:
I need a trustworthy view of the ingredients and batches available before making a purchasing decision.
Owner: Restaurant Manager. Source: UC.2.

entity.name: Checked Ingredient Information
entity.description: Manager-local review outcome from UC.1.9A to UC.1.10, including missing/uncertain fields, checked basis and decision to continue quantity review. Not a new external ICOM, inventory correction or purchase approval. If the manager defers, no continue outcome is issued. Maps to external manager responsibility P-F.1; the original recommendation basis is P-IO.09.

entity.name: Restaurant Manager Places Ingredient Order
entity.description: Team16 plan A is incorporated into this original use case by UC.1.9A, immediately after manager review. Recommendation data retains missing quantity and unknown expiration visibly; the manager checks/flags them before continuing to quantity revision and the existing explicit approval process. An unresolved basis may defer approval. Existing purchasing authority, supplier exchange and Action numbering are retained.

entity.name: Provide Authorized PANTRI Interaction State to Recovery Partner
entity.description: The PANTRI System shall provide Authorized PANTRI Interaction State to the Recovery Partner.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Rationale: Recovery coordination needs service and request/task authorization state to protect restaurant information and prevent unrelated collection responses from being accepted. The modeled recovery recipient therefore requires its own P-IO.17 obligation beyond the native PANTRI Staff statement. Upstream stakeholder requirements: SR.13, SR.12. MOP: Recovery Partner interaction-state agreement with the proposed scoped request/task/service matrix, paired with legitimate collection-information exchange completion. Proposed verification criterion: P-F.0 provides P-IO.17 to P-F.4 in the proposed recovery fixtures. An authorized available collection request/response exchange receives the applicable state and succeeds. An unrelated restaurant/request, unauthorized task or unavailable service receives denied/unavailable state without disclosing another request or changing its state. Compare outputs and exchange outcome with the independent matrix. This state authorizes PANTRI information interaction, not physical collection. Method: Recipient contract test and boundary inspection. Scenario scope: Authorized scoped recovery exchange; Unrelated restaurant/request; Unauthorized task; Unavailable service. Evaluation status: Planned, not executed. Fixture definitions are proposed review assumptions; operational agreement is not claimed. Requirement status: Draft.

entity.name: Calculate paired waste and availability measures
entity.description: The PANTRI System shall calculate waste per one hundred diner covers and ingredient stockout rate for the same declared restaurant ingredient scope and evaluation period.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Rationale: Both measures evaluate the waste and availability tradeoff. Higher-level source: SR.06; P-SFR.01. Allocated function: P-F.0.2.4. MOP: W=100*waste_mass_kg/diner_covers [kg/100 covers]; S=100*unavailable_valid_opportunities/all_valid_opportunities [% on 0-100 scale]. Criterion: independently recomputed values satisfy abs(actual-expected)<=max(1e-9,1e-9*abs(expected)), with absolute tolerance in each output unit. Include fractional 1/3 fixtures; zero or missing denominators return not calculable/null. Both measures must refer to the same restaurant, ingredient scope and evaluation period; scope association requires a separate integration check. Display rounding is separate from calculation precision. Method: Analysis and test. Verification status: Planned; bounded arithmetic tests do not establish full requirement or operational acceptance.

entity.name: Evaluate P-SFR.04 Provide Authorized PANTRI Interaction State to Ingredient Supplier

entity.name: Incomplete or stale ingredient records
entity.description: Condition: Inventory, usage, batch dates and waste observations can be missing, stale or inconsistent in units. Event: PANTRI produces advice from an incorrect or incomplete representation of usable stock and expected demand. Consequence: Managers may over-order, under-order or misinterpret the recommendation basis, undermining SR.01, SR.02, SR.05 and SR.06. Basis: The operational concept explicitly depends on reliable restaurant records; the current prototype uses controlled synthetic inputs rather than live feeds. Mitigation: Retain source and update context, distinguish unknown from zero, validate units and required fields, disclose material limitations and retain manager review. Evaluate missing, stale and boundary-date scenarios before expanding integrations. Trigger: An input lacks an agreed mandatory field, freshness condition or usable unit conversion. Residual risk: Validity checks cannot prove that an entered quantity matches the physical restaurant; independent record audits remain necessary. Status: Open. entity.name: Uncertain supplier or recovery responses

Event: PANTRI associates a response with the wrong transaction or presents an uncertain transaction as confirmed/resolved. Consequence: Managers or support staff may miss a supply or collection exception, affecting SR.04 and SR.11 and the operational coordination loop. Basis: Electronic participation is a documented assumption and the executable prototype currently uses a normal-path supplier stub. Mitigation: Require transaction association, preserve pending and exception states, record responsibility and follow-up, and test partial, delayed, duplicated and unrelated responses. Agree timeout and closure policies before baselining. Trigger: No valid associated response arrives within the agreed follow-up window or a response contradicts the retained order/request. Residual risk: PANTRI can represent and escalate the uncertainty but cannot guarantee physical delivery or collection. Status: Open. Qualitative ratings are preliminary, not measured probabilities.

Rationale: The P-IO.13 exchange supports SR.04, SR.11. The current recorded transaction state, confirmation or exception, associated follow-up and available delivery/pickup information. Pending, partial, delayed and resolved states remain distinguishable Upstream stakeholder requirements: SR.11, SR.04. MOP: Agreement of displayed order or collection-request state with the latest accepted, correctly associated supplier or recovery-partner event. Completeness of transaction, restaurant, ownership, exception state and follow-up information. Proposed verification criterion: Compare each prepared order and collection-request display with an independent transaction/event ledger. Preserve the correct restaurant and transaction association; distinguish awaiting, confirmed, partial, delayed and exceptional states as applicable. Missing responses remain pending. Each exception retains its responsible party and recorded follow-up/resolution; unassigned responsibility is explicit. An unrelated, duplicate or out-of-order event cannot silently overwrite another transaction or imply physical fulfillment. Use a declared proposed event-ordering/deduplication rule for these cases. Method: State-transition test and transaction-ledger inspection. Scenario scope: Supplier confirmation; Recovery response; No supplier/recovery response; Partial/delayed state; Collection exception; Unrelated/duplicate/out-of-order event; Unresolved follow-up. Evaluation status: Planned, not executed. Fixture definitions are proposed review assumptions; operational agreement is not claimed. Requirement status: Draft.

entity.name: Retain accepted ingredient events
entity.description: The PANTRI System shall retain the restaurant identifier, event identifier, quantity, unit, occurrence time and explicit unknown values of each accepted ingredient event.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Rationale: Reliable source records support subsequent planning. Higher-level source: SR.07, SR.08, SR.10; P-SFR.01. Allocated function: P-F.0.1.1. MOP: Field preservation rate = 100*F/N [%], where F counts applicable fields preserving the expected value, type, unit and explicit unknown state, and N is all applicable fields in a valid-event test manifest fixed before execution. Criterion: 100% within that declared receipt/usage/waste test set; N=0 is not computable. Invalid identifiers and units must be rejected without unauthorized mutation and are assessed separately. Compare independently prepared expected records, including explicit unknown values. Method: Inspection and test. Verification status: Planned; bounded prototype tests do not establish full requirement or operational acceptance.

entity.name: Evaluate 1.3.1 Demand, Order Approval, Recommendations & Alerts
entity.description: Planned evaluation for 1.3.1. Method: Bidirectional interface contract test and message inspection. MOP: Direction, recipient, association and required-field preservation across P-IO.01-.03 inbound and P-IO.08-.10, .13 and .17 outbound. Proposed criterion: In proposed fixtures, route manager requests/revisions/approvals from P-F.1 to P-F.0 and inventory/advice/metrics/status/interaction-state outputs back to the authorized manager boundary. Preserve restaurant and task, draft/order version, ingredient quantities/units or metric scope/period as applicable. Compare each direction with independent message fixtures. Accept a valid scoped exchange; reject a missing mandatory association or wrong restaurant/task without leakage or unintended approval. Every listed message category has at least one valid and one adverse case. Scenario scope: Valid request and information response; Valid revision and explicit approval; Missing draft/version; Wrong restaurant; Unauthorized task; Pending external status. Evidence to retain: declared fixture manifest, independent expected results, observed payload/state/output and discrepancy log. Status: Not Run. No execution result or operational agreement is claimed.

stringAttribute.value: Not Run

entity.name: Distinguish expiration information
entity.description: The PANTRI System shall classify recorded ingredient batches relative to the declared expiration horizon while preserving unknown expiration dates as unknown.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Rationale: Unknown dates cannot support use-first assurances. Higher-level source: SR.05; P-SFR.01. Allocated function: P-F.0.2.3. MOP: Expiration classification accuracy and unknown-date false-safe count. Proposed verification criterion: Test before, on and after horizon boundaries and null dates; each class matches an independent date oracle and no unknown date becomes safe. Method: Analysis and test. Verification status: Planned; no implementation or operational acceptance result is inferred from the architecture model.

entity.name: Accept Purchase Quantity Revisions
entity.description: The PANTRI System shall accept Purchase Quantity Revisions from the Restaurant Manager.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Rationale: SR.03A requires manager control of proposed quantities before approval. A revision must remain associated with its restaurant and draft version so that an unrelated edit cannot silently change the purchase decision. Upstream stakeholder requirements: SR.03A. MOP: P-IO.02 accepted-edit field/version agreement and invalid-edit rejection at the P-F.1-to-P-F.0 input boundary. Proposed verification criterion: For the proposed edit fixture, accept a Restaurant Manager revision containing restaurant, draft/version, ingredient, finite nonnegative quantity and unit; a 4-to-5 kg edit changes only the referenced unapproved draft. Reject a negative/nonfinite quantity, missing unit, unrelated draft or superseded version; the previous accepted draft remains intact. An accepted revision neither approves nor transmits an order. All prepared applicable cases meet the independent expected-state fixture. Method: Boundary and state-transition test. Scenario scope: 4-to-5 kg edit; Zero quantity; Negative or nonfinite quantity; Missing unit; Wrong/superseded draft; Repeated edit. Evaluation status: Planned, not executed. Fixture definitions are proposed review assumptions; operational agreement is not claimed. Requirement status: Draft.

entity.name: Accept Planning and Information Requests
entity.description: The PANTRI System shall accept Planning and Information Requests from the Restaurant Manager.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Rationale: Manager requests identify the restaurant, ingredient scope, period and information task needed to produce relevant inventory, advice, expiration and performance views under SR.01, SR.02, SR.05 and SR.06. Requesting information must not itself authorize purchasing. Upstream stakeholder requirements: SR.01, SR.05, SR.06, SR.02. MOP: P-IO.01 field-preservation rate, valid-request acceptance rate and invalid-request rejection rate at the P-F.1-to-P-F.0 control boundary. Proposed verification criterion: Using the proposed request schema, accept a manager request carrying restaurant ID, selected ingredient IDs, task type and period; preserve supplied demand context. Reject missing restaurant, unsupported task or unauthorized scope without changing accepted operational records. Compare accepted fields with the independent input fixture. The valid information request produces no approval or purchase transmission. All prepared applicable cases meet these expectations. Method: Boundary test and inspection. Scenario scope: Valid inventory/advice/expiration/performance request; Missing restaurant ID; Unsupported task; Wrong restaurant scope; Repeated information request. Evaluation status: Planned, not executed. Fixture definitions are proposed review assumptions; operational agreement is not claimed. Requirement status: Draft.

entity.name: Loss of restaurant boundaries or record integrity during access and recovery
entity.description: Condition: The intended three-restaurant service requires role-sensitive access and restoration of linked records after interruption. Event: A user accesses another restaurant's records, or restoration/export loses an approval, correction or transaction relationship. Consequence: Operational evidence becomes exposed or untrustworthy, affecting SR.13, SR.14 and SR.15. Basis: Authentication, persistent storage and production recovery are outside the current offline UC.1 implementation. Mitigation: Define the restaurant/role/action matrix; evaluate denied and legitimate tasks together. Restore and export a known linked reference set and compare required fields and relationships. Record restoration time without inventing an agreed recovery-time threshold. Trigger: Any unexpected access grant or mismatch in a confirmed reference record or relationship. Residual risk: Prepared tests provide bounded evidence; operational monitoring and stakeholder agreement on recovery objectives remain necessary. Status: Open. Qualitative ratings are preliminary, not measured probabilities.

entity.name: System Operation & Support Information
entity.description: The PANTRI System shall interface with the PANTRI Staff through the System Operation & Support Information.

stringAttribute.value: Draft

Rationale: Support staff need scoped policy/command input and trustworthy exception, availability, recovery and handover output. Preserving command authority and restaurant context prevents support actions from becoming an uncontrolled route across restaurant boundaries. Upstream stakeholder requirements: SR.11, SR.15, SR.14, SR.13, SR.12. MOP: P-IO.07 inbound command/policy scope and version agreement; P-IO.15-.17 outbound monitoring, recovered/exported-record and interaction-state agreement. Proposed verification criterion: In proposed P-F.5-to-P-F.0 fixtures, policies/commands preserve authorized actor, restaurant/task scope, version/effective context and referenced recovery/export set. Reverse fixtures preserve exception/workflow ID, observation time/state and recovered/exported record references as applicable. Compare both directions with independent policy, monitoring and record fixtures. Valid authorized exchanges succeed; missing scope, wrong role or unrelated restaurant is denied. Command acceptance is distinct from completed restoration/export; missing monitoring observations do not imply availability. Method: Bidirectional interface contract test and support-record inspection. Scenario scope: Valid policy and monitoring exchange; Authorized recovery/export; Missing scope; Wrong role/restaurant; Missing observation; Unavailable service. Evaluation status: Planned, not executed. Fixture definitions are proposed review assumptions; operational agreement is not claimed. Requirement status: Draft.
